problems.title: Divisibility of a repeated three-digit block
problems.question: Which of 13,17,19,21 divides 199199?
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, keep the required domain, and verify every possible case.
steps: The factorization contains 13. It contains neither 17 nor 19, and 21 requires a factor 3, absent because the digit sum is 38.

problems.title: Symmetry of an absolute-value quadratic
problems.question: Which symmetry must $f(x)=2x^2-8|x|+3$ have?
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, keep the required domain, and verify every possible case.
formulas: An even function satisfies f(−x)=f(x).
steps: Both x² and |x| are unchanged on replacing x by −x. Thus the graph is symmetric in the y axis.

problems.title: Bound a cube root
problems.question: Which unit interval contains $\sqrt[3]{30}+4$?
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, keep the required domain, and verify every possible case.
steps: Take increasing real cube roots to get 3<∛30<4. Adding 4 yields 7<∛30+4<8.

problems.title: A chord subtending a thirty-degree angle
problems.question: Secants MCA and MDB pass through an exterior point M. AB is a diameter, CD=10 cm, and angle CBM=30°. Find the circle radius.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, keep the required domain, and verify every possible case.
formulas: Because B,D,M are collinear on the secant, $\angle CBD=30^\circ$; chord $CD=2R\sin\angle CBD$.
steps: The inscribed angle at B subtends CD. Therefore 10=2R sin30°=R.

problems.title: All third sides of an acute triangle
problems.question: For which real x is a triangle with sides 3,4,x acute?
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, keep the required domain, and verify every possible case.
formulas: Each squared side must be smaller than the sum of the other squared sides, together with positive lengths.
steps: The nontrivial conditions are $16<9+x^2$ and $x^2<9+16$. They give x>√7 and x<5.
This interval already satisfies the triangle inequality 1<x<7; the remaining acute condition is automatic.

problems.title: Triangles on two parallel lines
problems.question: One of two parallel lines has one chosen point and the other has five. Count triangles with vertices among these points.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, keep the required domain, and verify every possible case.
formulas: Each triangle must use the lone point and two of the five collinear points.
steps: The count is $\binom52=10$. Every such choice is noncollinear because the lines are distinct and parallel.

problems.title: Chicken feed and proportional rates
problems.question: Eight chickens eat 3 kg of corn in six days. How many days do three chickens need to eat 24 kg?
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, keep the required domain, and verify every possible case.
formulas: One chicken’s daily rate is $3/(8\cdot6)=1/16$ kg.
steps: Three chickens eat 3/16 kg per day. The time is 24/(3/16)=128 days.

problems.title: Count positive defined sequence terms
problems.question: How many terms of $a_n=(20.4-n)/(n^2-100)$ are positive for natural n?
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, keep the required domain, and verify every possible case.
formulas: The numerator changes sign at 20.4 and denominator at n=10 for positive indices.
steps: For n=1 through 9 the numerator is positive and denominator negative. At n=10 the formula is undefined.
Both are positive at n=11 through 20, giving ten positive terms. For n≥21, only the numerator is negative.
problems.note: The displayed formula does not define a term at n=10. The count concerns the other, defined indices; formally the sequence needs that missing term specified or excluded.

problems.title: Prism faces from its space diagonals
problems.question: A prism has 130 space diagonals. Find its face count.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, keep the required domain, and verify every possible case.
formulas: An n-gonal prism has $D=n(n-3)$ space diagonals and F=n+2 faces.
steps: Each vertex connects by a space diagonal to n−3 vertices in the opposite base. Counting all 2n vertices and dividing by 2 gives n(n−3).
problems.note: Here “prism diagonals” means space diagonals, excluding diagonals contained in faces, the standard convention used by the choices.

problems.title: A triangle inside a right trapezoid
problems.question: ABCD is a right trapezoid with right angles at A,B, bases AD=8,BC=4 and CD=5. Find area ACD.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, keep the required domain, and verify every possible case.
formulas: Height $h=\sqrt{CD^2-(AD-BC)^2}$; triangle area $=AD\,h/2$.

problems.title: A ratio in an arithmetic progression
problems.question: A positive arithmetic progression satisfies a₃=75% of a₄. What percentage of a₁₀ is a₄?
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, keep the required domain, and verify every possible case.
steps: $4(a_1+2d)=3(a_1+3d)$ gives a₁=d. Hence aₙ=nd.
The ratio a₄/a₁₀=4/10=40%.

problems.title: A radical equation with an endpoint root
problems.question: Find the smallest root of $x^2\sqrt{x+1}-4\sqrt{x+1}=0$.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, keep the required domain, and verify every possible case.
formulas: Domain x≥−1; factor $\sqrt{x+1}(x^2-4)=0$.
steps: The radical is zero at x=−1. The quadratic factor gives x=±2, but −2 is outside the domain.
The valid roots are −1 and 2; the smaller is −1.

problems.title: Repeatedly replacing milk with water
problems.question: A full 40-litre barrel initially contains milk. Each operation replaces 10 litres of well-mixed contents with water. After how many operations does water first exceed milk?
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, keep the required domain, and verify every possible case.
formulas: Each operation retains 3/4 of the current milk; milk after n steps is $40(3/4)^n$.
steps: Water exceeds milk iff milk is less than 20 litres. After two operations the milk is 22.5 litres; after three it is 16.875 litres.
Therefore three is the first successful count.

problems.title: Circumcircle area with arithmetic-progression angles
problems.question: Triangle angles form an arithmetic progression. The middle-length side is 15 cm. Find the circumcircle area.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, keep the required domain, and verify every possible case.
formulas: The middle angle is 60°; sine rule $b=2R\sin60^\circ$.
steps: Angle sum 180° makes the middle angle 60°. The middle side corresponds to it, so R=15/√3=5√3.
The circle area is πR²=75π cm².

problems.title: A difference of sets with an empty intersection
problems.question: A consists of positive multiples of 4; B consists of positive integers congruent to 3 modulo 4; C consists of positive integers below 100 ending in 3. Find the size of $(A\cap B)\setminus C$.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, keep the required domain, and verify every possible case.
formulas: An integer cannot have two different remainders modulo 4.
steps: A∩B is empty. Removing any C from the empty set still gives the empty set.

problems.title: Even and odd positions of a geometric progression
problems.question: A geometric progression has a nonzero first term and an even number of terms. The even-position sum is seven times the odd-position sum. Find its ratio q.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, keep the required domain, and verify every possible case.
formulas: $b_{2j}=q b_{2j-1}$, hence $S_{\rm even}=q S_{\rm odd}$.
steps: The odd-position sum is $b_1(1+q^2+\cdots+q^{2m-2})$, nonzero for real q and b₁≠0.
Therefore qSodd=7Sodd can be divided by Sodd, giving q=7.
problems.note: As usual for a specified geometric ratio, the progression is assumed nonzero. If every term were zero, the sum condition would not determine a ratio.

problems.title: Oddness and period four
problems.question: f is odd with period 4, and $f(199)^3+64=0$. Find f(2021).
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, keep the required domain, and verify every possible case.
formulas: Periodicity gives f(x+4k)=f(x); oddness gives f(−x)=−f(x).
steps: f(199)=−4. Since 199 is congruent to −1 modulo 4, f(−1)=−4 and f(1)=4.
2021 is congruent to 1 modulo 4, so f(2021)=4.

problems.title: Angle between centroid vectors
problems.question: A=(2,1),B=(1,5),C=(3,3), and O is the centroid. Find the cosine between OA and OB.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, keep the required domain, and verify every possible case.
formulas: Centroid coordinates are coordinate averages; $\cos\theta=(u\cdot v)/(|u||v|)$.
steps: O=(2,3), so OA=(0,−2) and OB=(−1,2). Their dot product is −4 and length product is 2√5.
Thus cos theta=−2/√5.

problems.title: Height above a right triangle’s circumcentre
problems.question: S is 17 cm from each vertex of a right triangle with legs 18 and 24 cm. Find its distance to the triangle plane.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, keep the required domain, and verify every possible case.
formulas: Right-triangle circumradius is half the hypotenuse; $17^2=h^2+R^2$.
steps: The hypotenuse is 30 and R=15. The equal-distance point projects to the circumcentre.

problems.title: Combine exponents by multiplication and division
problems.question: $2^x=112,2^y=6,2^z=42$. Find x+y−z.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, keep the required domain, and verify every possible case.
steps: The right side is 112×6/42=16=2⁴. Thus x+y−z=4.

problems.title: Translate a parabola
problems.question: Translate $y=x^2-4x+1$ by vector (6,5) to obtain $y=(x+a)^2+b$. Find a+b.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, keep the required domain, and verify every possible case.
formulas: A translation (u,v) gives $g(x)=f(x-u)+v$.
steps: The original is (x−2)²−3. Translating gives (x−8)²+2.
Thus a=−8,b=2 and a+b=−6.

problems.title: A logarithm with a squared base parameter
problems.question: For which a is $y=\log_{a^2}x$ decreasing?
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, keep the required domain, and verify every possible case.
formulas: A real logarithmic function decreases iff its base lies strictly between zero and one.
steps: Require 0<a²<1, which is equivalent to −1<a<1 with a≠0. The excluded values also prevent base 0 or 1.

problems.title: Remove two cones from a cylinder
problems.question: Two cones have the cylinder’s bases and their common vertex at the axis midpoint. Find remaining-volume/cylinder-volume.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, keep the required domain, and verify every possible case.
formulas: Cone volume is one third of base area times height.
steps: Each cone has half the cylinder height, so each volume is 1/6 of the cylinder’s. Their interiors are disjoint and their sum is 1/3.
The remaining fraction is 1−1/3=2/3.

problems.title: Square-to-hexagon area ratio
problems.question: A square’s circumradius equals a regular hexagon’s inradius. Find square area divided by hexagon area.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, keep the required domain, and verify every possible case.
formulas: For common radius r, square area $=2r^2$; hexagon side $=2r/\sqrt3$ and area $=3\sqrt3s^2/2$.
steps: The hexagon area is 2√3r². Dividing gives 1/√3=√3/3.

problems.title: Uniform probability in an interval
problems.question: A number is chosen uniformly from [−1,3]. Find probability it is positive.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, keep the required domain, and verify every possible case.
formulas: Probability = favourable length / total length.
steps: The positive portion has length 3 and the whole interval length 4. Endpoints have zero probability.

problems.title: Recover an acute cosine from a sum
problems.question: $\cos y=1/7$, $\cos(x+y)=-11/14$, with x,y acute. Find cos x.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, keep the required domain, and verify every possible case.
formulas: $\sin y=4\sqrt3/7$; cosine addition formula.
steps: Let c=cos x∈(0,1). The addition formula gives $2c-8\sqrt3\sqrt{1-c^2}=-11$.
Move the radical to the other side and square: $192(1-c^2)=(2c+11)^2$, hence $196c^2+44c-71=0$.
The roots are 1/2 and −71/98; only 1/2 is acute. Substitution checks it: $1/14-(\sqrt3/2)(4\sqrt3/7)=-11/14$.

problems.title: A pyramid with three perpendicular edges
problems.question: The three face angles at a pyramid vertex are right angles; the three adjoining edges are 6,8,10 cm. Find its volume.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, keep the required domain, and verify every possible case.
formulas: A tetrahedron with three perpendicular edges a,b,c has $V=abc/6$.
steps: Use the 6-by-8 right triangle as base, area 24, and perpendicular height 10. Then V=24×10/3=80 cm³.

problems.title: A sector from its chord
problems.question: A circle has radius 2√2 cm. A sector AOB has chord AB=4 cm. Find sector area.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, keep the required domain, and verify every possible case.
formulas: $AB=2R\sin(\theta/2)$; sector area $=R^2\theta/2$ in radians.
steps: The chord gives sin(theta/2)=1/√2. The minor central angle is π/2, yielding area 8×(π/2)/2=2π.
The same chord also bounds a major sector with angle 3π/2 and area 6π.
problems.answer: Minor sector: $2\pi\text{ cm}^2$; major sector: $6\pi\text{ cm}^2$.
problems.note: The source does not explicitly say minor sector. The usual minor-sector reading gives 2π; allowing the major sector adds 6π.

problems.title: Dilute salt water
problems.question: 30 kg of seawater containing 4% salt is mixed with 50 kg of fresh water. Find the resulting salt percentage.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, keep the required domain, and verify every possible case.
formulas: Salt mass is unchanged; concentration = salt mass / total mass.
steps: The salt mass is 30×0.04=1.2 kg, and the final mass is 80 kg. The fraction is 1.2/80=0.015.

problems.title: Area of a cyclic trapezoid
problems.question: ABCD is a cyclic trapezoid with bases BC,AD and centre O. Angle COD=alpha, tan(alpha/2)=3/4, and the midline is 8. Find its area.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, keep the required domain, and verify every possible case.
formulas: A cyclic trapezoid is isosceles. With symmetric side endpoints on its circle, $h/m=\tan(\alpha/2)$; area $=mh$.
steps: To derive the ratio, write right-side vertices C=(Rcos u,Rsin u), D=(Rcos v,Rsin v). Then $m=R(\cos u+\cos v)$ and $h=R(\sin u-\sin v)$.
Sum-to-product identities give $h/m=\tan((u-v)/2)=\tan(\alpha/2)=3/4$. Thus h=8×3/4=6.
The area is 8×6=48.

problems.title: Exactly six integer square-root inputs
problems.question: For which a does $\sqrt x\le a$ have exactly six integer solutions?
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, keep the required domain, and verify every possible case.
formulas: If a≥0, the solution is $0\le x\le a^2$.
steps: The six integer solutions must be 0,1,2,3,4,5. This occurs iff 5≤a²<6.
Taking nonnegative square roots gives √5≤a<√6.

problems.title: Overlap with a rotated right triangle
problems.question: An isosceles right triangle has legs 2√3. Rotate it 45° about the right-angle vertex. Find the overlap area.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, keep the required domain, and verify every possible case.
formulas: Let leg length L and place the original at $x\ge0,y\ge0,x+y\le L$. The rotated triangle adds $y\ge x$ and $y\le L/\sqrt2$ in this quadrant.
steps: For 0≤y≤L/2, the overlap width is y. For L/2≤y≤L/√2, it is L−y.
The area is $\int_0^{L/2}y\,dy+\int_{L/2}^{L/\sqrt2}(L-y)dy=L^2(1/\sqrt2-1/2)$.
With L²=12 this is 6(√2−1). Clockwise rotation gives the same area by reflection symmetry.

problems.title: Extrema using sine as a new variable
problems.question: Find the maximum and minimum of $2+\sin x-\cos^2x$.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, keep the required domain, and verify every possible case.
formulas: Set t=sin x∈[−1,1]; cos²x=1−t².
steps: The expression becomes $1+t+t^2=(t+1/2)^2+3/4$. Its minimum is 3/4 at t=−1/2.
This convex quadratic has its maximum on the interval at an endpoint: values 1 at t=−1 and 3 at t=1.

problems.title: A vertical plane cuts a corner off a regular pyramid
problems.question: A regular triangular pyramid has base side 4√3 and base dihedral angle 60°. A plane perpendicular to the base bisects two base sides. Find the cut-off triangular pyramid volume.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, keep the required domain, and verify every possible case.
formulas: Base inradius r=2; height $H=r\tan60^\circ$; pyramid volume $=BH/3$.
steps: The base altitude is 6 and area 12√3. The apex projects to the centroid, distance 4 from the corner A along its base median. Hence H=2√3 and the full volume is 24.
The vertical cutting plane is over the midpoint segment, distance 3 from A along that median. It meets the edge from A to the apex at fraction 3/4 of that edge.
The corner pyramid’s base triangle has 1/4 of the original base area and its top has height 3H/4. Its volume is $(1/4)(3/4)24=9/2$.

problems.title: A parameter in an exponential trigonometric equation
problems.question: Find all a for which $4^{|\cos x|}-(a+5)2^{|\cos x|}+3a+6=0$ has a real solution.
problems.idea: Use the relevant formula, keep the required domain, and verify every possible case.
steps: The quadratic factors as $(t-3)(t-a-2)=0$. The root t=3 is outside [1,2].
Thus a solution exists iff a+2∈[1,2], or −1≤a≤0. Every t in this interval is attained by some x.
